audit.whatIsWrong: Difficulty prose treated Riftwalk as a cooldown problem.
audit.why: Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s — it is never on cooldown. The real constraint is that repeat casts cost escalating Mana, which is what Riot's description states.
audit.corrected: mid and spikes[1] now key the punish to his mana bar, not to a cooldown.

audit.why: Spikes already track the real breakpoints: pre-6 helplessness, level 6 Riftwalk, and the Rod of Ages/Rylai timing that lets him kite.
audit.corrected: Left as written; only cooldown detail added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive kit interaction was never stated: Null Sphere shield absorbs magic damage only.
audit.why: Riot's text: "granting a temporary shield that absorbs magic damage". Aatrox's Q chain is physical, so the shield is irrelevant to his burst — Kassadin's only genuine interrupt value is the channel interrupt on Null Sphere.
audit.corrected: early now states the shield does nothing against a physical Q chain.

audit.whatIsWrong: No concrete punishable cooldown was named.
audit.why: Force Pulse (E) is 21/20/19/18/17s — by far his longest basic cooldown and his only self-peel pre-6.
audit.corrected: spikes[0] and mid now give the 21s number and tell you to trade once it is spent.

edits.before: Peak dominance: pre-6 Kassadin has no Riftwalk escape, so every time he steps up to last-hit, E in and land a full Q chain. Deny him CS and snowball the lane.
edits.after: Peak dominance: pre-6 Kassadin has no escape, and Force Pulse (E) is 21s at rank 1 — once that cone slow is spent, E in and land a full Q chain. Deny CS and snowball.

edits.before: His Riftwalk (R) blink gives him an out, but it costs mana and stacks damage against him — bait one blink, then W (Infernal Chains) or Q3 knockup to catch the follow-up before he can chain them.
edits.after: Riftwalk (R) is a 5s cooldown, so you never catch it down — you catch him out of mana, since repeat blinks cost escalating Mana. Bait one, then W (Infernal Chains) or Q3 knockup before he affords the second.

edits.before: You crush the early game. Kassadin is one of the weakest pre-6 laners in the game — melee with no escape, poor waveclear, and he only wants to farm. Levels 1-3 you can walk up and E-Q him almost for free every time he goes for a minion. Set up a slow-push and force him to CS under your threat; deny him and the whole matchup is decided before he spikes.
edits.after: You crush the early game. Kassadin is one of the weakest pre-6 laners — melee, no escape, poor waveclear. Null Sphere (Q) is his only interrupt, and its shield absorbs magic damage only, so it does nothing about your physical Q chain. Walk up and E-Q him every time he steps to a minion; slow-push, force him to CS under threat, and the lane is decided before he spikes.

edits.before: Through 4-6 you remain firmly ahead as long as you keep the pressure on. At 6 his Riftwalk finally gives him a blink escape, but each cast burns mana and adds a stacking cost, so bait the first one and immediately catch him — W to pin, Q3 to knock up — before he can blink twice. World Ender turns any caught Kassadin into a kill. Every plate and kill you take here is banked against his scaling.
edits.after: Through 4-6 you stay ahead if you keep the pressure on. Force Pulse (E) is his only real punish and it is 21s at rank 1, so trade the moment it is spent. At 6 Riftwalk gives him an out on a 5s cooldown, but each repeat blink costs escalating Mana — bait the first and immediately catch him: W to pin, Q3 to knock up. World Ender turns any caught Kassadin into a kill.

edits.before: Track his mana so you can dive right after a Riftwalk
edits.after: Track his mana — each repeat Riftwalk costs far more

edits.before: Even at 6 you win — bait one Riftwalk and catch the follow-up before he chains blinks.
edits.after: Even at 6 you win — bait one Riftwalk, then kill him before he affords another.

notes: The _missing file claims Null Sphere is a channel your World Ender cancels — that is backwards: Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels, it is not one, and World Ender has no interrupt. Not used. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag that Riot's own description does not support (it describes a drag + slow only), so no grounding claim was made anywhere in this slice.
